subject.title: [Feature] Telegram Inline Query Support (@botname in any chat)

question: Should OpenClaw add opt-in Telegram inline-query support inside the bundled Telegram plugin, and what authorization, cache, session, and execution defaults should it use?
rationale: The implementation path is clear from the Telegram plugin boundary, but routing arbitrary-chat inline query text into agents changes authorization, privacy, caching, and execution behavior that automation should not choose alone.

options.title: Approve constrained opt-in inline mode
options.body: Add an explicit inline-query opt-in with account-level authorization, personal/no-cache defaults for user-specific results, bounded agent execution, docs, tests, and live Telegram proof.

options.title: Defer behind arbitrary-chat ingress design
options.body: Keep this open until Guest Mode and bot-to-bot security decisions settle, then implement inline queries using the shared approved boundary.

options.title: Decline built-in inline mode for now
options.body: Leave inline-query support out of the bundled Telegram plugin and document that operators need a separate bot until OpenClaw has a safer extension seam.

recommendation.title: Approve constrained opt-in inline mode
recommendation.body: Add an explicit inline-query opt-in with account-level authorization, personal/no-cache defaults for user-specific results, bounded agent execution, docs, tests, and live Telegram proof.

likelyOwner.reason: Current Telegram handler/config blame plus broader channel configuration history make this the best available owner for the product/security boundary decision.
